findings.claim: The Prepared quote in ripple/section 09: "fallen out of favor as newer iterations improved design"
findings.note: Source verbatim: "This specific product has fallen out of favor as more modern iterations improved on the original design, adding features like retaining strips." Page quotes it in quotes but with 'newer' instead of 'more modern' and 'improved design' instead of 'improved on the original design'. Not word-for-word.

findings.claim: Early adoption by 75th Rangers and 101st Airborne in 2000-2001
findings.note: JTA does not give dates for the elite-unit adoption. It says 'In 2000, he took the bandage to Fort Sam Houston... Soon his company, First Care, was selling the bandage for use by elite units, including the 75th Rangers and the 101st Airborne. Three years later the bandage was certified for standard use.' '2000-2001' is a reasonable inference, not a sourced date; putting it in the infobox as if sourced overstates JTA.

findings.claim: Pima County sheriff's deputies used the Israeli bandage to treat 10 of the 19 casualties in the 47 minutes before paramedics arrived (Tucson)
findings.note: JEMS: 'During the 47 minutes that deputies were with the injured at the scene, they treated 10 of the 19 injured patients... controlled bleeding, provided rescue breathing and chest compressions, deployed hemostatic agents, bandaged numerous wounds.' JEMS' IFAK listing includes 'Two emergency compression bandages' but does not name the manufacturer. NPR confirms an 'Israeli bandage' was in the IFAK. No source says the Israeli bandage was used on all 10/19; the page's phrasing implies stronger causation than sources support.

findings.claim: The frustration built up over years of reserve duty; in 1993 the idea 'was invented'
findings.note: JTA supports the reserve-duty framing ('As the years wore on through monthlong stints in the Israeli reserves'). However, Jorisch explicitly says 'After his military discharge, Bar-Natan began tinkering with alternatives' — a soft cross-source disagreement the page does not acknowledge. Page's choice (JTA) is defensible.

findings.claim: In the 1980s Bar-Natan went through medic training in the IDF (drafted at age 26)
findings.note: JTA: 'immigrated to Israel in 1979 and was drafted into the military in 1983' — 1983 minus a 1957-born (implicit) puts him at ~26, consistent.

JTA verbatim: 'the equivalent of up to 30 pounds of pressure over the pad by wrapping it in the opposite direction of the initial wrap.'

notes_summary: Page holds. Two moderate findings (paraphrased The Prepared quote in quotes; 2000-2001 elite-unit date is inferred not sourced). One minor Tucson finding (implied causation between Israeli-bandage and all 10/19 treatments is stronger than sources support). No factual falsehoods, no cross-language contradictions, no phantom device (rule 176 satisfied: real patent, real factory, real millions of units, real operational use).
